title: Gin and Tonic: A Better Balance at Home
steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Add gin.
Top gently with tonic water.
Garnish with lime and serve.
tip: Use plenty of cold ice and add tonic last to preserve carbonation.

title: How to Choose a Wine for a Dinner Party
points: Think about the main dish, not every side.
Choose a versatile style when guests have different preferences.
Keep one white and one red option if the menu is mixed.
Serve wine at a comfortable temperature and avoid overthinking the pairing.

title: Moscow Mule: An Easy Three-Ingredient Classic
steps: Fill a mug or tall glass with ice.
Add vodka and fresh lime juice.
Top with ginger beer.
Stir briefly and garnish with lime.
tip: Fresh lime makes a noticeable difference.

title: What Makes Bourbon Different from Other Whiskey?
points: Bourbon is a type of American whiskey.
Its grain recipe must contain at least 51% corn.
It is aged in new charred oak containers.
Flavor often includes vanilla, caramel, oak, and baking-spice notes.

title: Paloma: A Bright Grapefruit Tequila Drink
steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Add tequila and lime juice.
Top with grapefruit soda.
Stir gently and garnish.
tip: A pinch of salt can soften bitterness and brighten the citrus.

title: A Beginner’s Guide to Sparkling Wine
points: Sparkling wine comes in many styles, from dry to sweet.
Look for dryness terms on the label when comparing bottles.
Serve well chilled.
Use sparkling wine for celebrations, appetizers, brunch, or simple food pairings.

title: Rum and Ginger: A Simple Highball
ingredients: 4–5 oz ginger beer or ginger ale
steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Add rum and lime juice.
Top with ginger beer or ginger ale.
Stir gently and serve.
tip: Choose ginger beer for more spice or ginger ale for a softer drink.

title: How Much Wine, Beer and Spirits to Buy for a Party
points: Start with the number of adult guests and event length.
Offer water and nonalcoholic drinks throughout the event.
Choose a smaller, versatile mix rather than too many categories.
Plan transportation and encourage responsible consumption.

title: French 75: A Sparkling Citrus Cocktail
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice.
Strain into a flute or coupe.
Top with sparkling wine.
Garnish with lemon peel if desired.
tip: Keep the sparkling wine chilled and add it only after shaking.

title: Tequila Basics: Blanco, Reposado and Añejo
points: Blanco is typically unaged or lightly rested and highlights agave flavor.
Reposado spends time in oak and often gains vanilla and spice notes.
Añejo is aged longer, producing deeper oak-driven character.
The best style depends on whether you plan to sip or mix.

title: Negroni: The Classic 1-1-1 Formula
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir until chilled.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
Garnish with orange peel.
tip: The equal-parts formula makes this classic easy to remember.

title: Easy Cheese and Wine Pairing Ideas
points: Fresh cheeses often work well with crisp whites or sparkling wine.
Hard aged cheeses can pair with fuller reds or richer whites.
Blue cheese often benefits from a sweeter wine contrast.
When unsure, sparkling wine is a flexible choice for a mixed cheese board.
